note: Lolo's lines, per level. Dialogue-node text follows Game Design section 6; the choice wording is the design's verbatim, because the three answers are what the player is choosing between and paraphrasing them changes the choice.

level_1.greeting: You're holding her brush. Press R and draw — anything you draw, this place believes.
level_1.climb: That wall is taller than you. Draw a way up it, or draw something that climbs.

node.speaker: Lolo
node.context: The gorge. Her hanging bridge is rotted clean away — nothing left but the posts and a bit of rope.

choices.pragmatist: Let's just climb down and go around.
choices.protector: I'll carve us a new path.

routes.artist: Then we build it the way she did. Plank by plank — draw them and set them in the gaps.
routes.pragmatist: Down we go, then. Draw something that can hold a wall — a spider would do it.
routes.protector: The dead tree, then. Draw an edge, pick it up with E, and swing with F.

memory.title: A memory
lines: She is younger here, and the light is the same gold it is now.
Lola is painting this bridge — the ropes first, then the planks, one at a time, humming something you almost remember.
She looks up from the canvas, straight out of it, and smiles like she knew you would come this way.

level_1.cave: There's a cave down there. Too dark to see into — we'd need to bring our own light. Not today.
level_1.arrival: That's her overlook. Go on — she'd want you to see it.
